story: The flood (SERIES.md episode 9; arc 3, The Flood)
people: The scoffer (characters.json, the invented ringleader of the mockers, DRAFT until his reference sheet is reviewed) opens on screen at the shut door, begging in our own words (kind story, no reference: Genesis records no word of the people outside, and none is presented as Scripture); he shrugs off the animals, runs for the hills and stands on the last rock at the climax. Noah (DRAFT) appears by reference in two shots at the ark's door (wardrobe 'ark') and never speaks: Genesis gives him no words before the flood is over. Elsewhere his family and the people of the valley are anonymous, seen from behind or in silhouette. God is never shown: His Genesis 7:4 is a deep voice-over over the storm. No establishing shot: every scene is acted by people. The Keeper only for the insight, the comment question and the close. This plan passes plan_check only once Noah and the scoffer are APPROVED.
beats: structure bible-story-short (script.beats): cold_open s-door (the scoffer pounds on the shut door in the first rain and begs Noah to open), then God's Genesis 7:4 (s-voice, voice-over: seven days, then forty days of rain); stake and open loop (seven days earlier he was still laughing; one week, one open door: would anyone believe?); escalation in three rising steps of the flood against the valley, acted, each ending on a hook (the animals come and the family goes in, and the Lord shut him in; the fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven, and the scoffer runs for the hills; the waters bear up the ark and cover the hills, one last peak); acted climax s-peak and s-drift (the scoffer on the last rock watches the ark float past) carrying Genesis 7:23 'and Noah only remained alive'; payoff (Genesis 7:24, the family safe inside, the shut door held); keeper_close (insight: seven more days with the door open, and the Lord, not Noah, shut it; comment question; part 10).

narration.text: Seven days before that cry, the ark stood finished on the hillside, and the very same man was still laughing at it.
One week of warning. One open door, and room inside. Would anyone outside believe it before the sky broke?
There went in two and two unto Noah into the ark, the male and the female, as God had commanded Noah.
They descended from the mountains by themselves. Lions beside frightened sheep. Birds in pairs settling along the roof. Nobody herded them.
The crowd stopped laughing for a moment. Then the scoffer shrugged, and the music in the camps started again.
And Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.
and the Lord shut him in.
And once that door was shut, no hand on earth could open it again.
the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.
Water from below and water from above. The ground split, springs burst through the camps, and the rain did not stop, day or night.
Now the whole valley stampeded toward higher ground, dragging children and animals up the slopes. And the scoffer ran with them.
And the flood was forty days upon the earth; and the waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lift up above the earth.
The ark that sat in the dust for years groaned, lifted, and floated. Fists pounded on its hull as it drifted away from them.
And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered.
Hill after hill went under. The last of them crowded onto one bare peak, and still the water kept climbing.
On the last rock, the man who laughed watched the ark he mocked float past him in the rain.
and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.
And the waters prevailed upon the earth an hundred and fifty days.
Inside, eight people and a vessel full of animals, alone on an ocean with no shoreline. The door that was shut had held.
Most miss this: after the ark was finished, God gave seven more days with the door open. And Noah never shut it. The Lord did.
If that door were open today, who would you call inside? Tell me in the comments.
The full story is in the long video. Part ten tomorrow: The dove and the rainbow.

shots.speaker: scoffer
shots.line: Noah! Open the door! The water is coming up, and we were wrong. Open it, old man!
